messages:
sara:seeing a sharp p95 bump across rack-12 GPU nodes during the 12:00-12:10 batching window. p95 jumped from ~45ms to ~420ms. :eyes:

kyle:noticed same in the dashboards, looks east-west only, north-south fine. packets_retrans up on a few nodes.

maria:can you paste a small snippet of the tc/ifstats? also which cluster and rack?

sara:us-west2-prod-gpu-rack-12. quick ifstat from node gpu-12-03: 
```
rxpck/s: 1200  txpck/s: 1195  rxerr/s: 0  txerr/s: 0
rx_drop/s: 0  tx_drop/s: 15
```
but `ethtool -S` shows tx_dropped increasing on mlx5 interface.

ben:15 tx_drops aligns with driver-level queue drops. could be QP saturation on the RDMA path. any ib stats?

kyle:ran `ibperf` probe between gpu-12-03 and gpu-12-07, small bursts show increased latency and occasional packet loss. ib_port_counters show remote_qp_err increments.

infra-bot:automated alert — east-west p95 > 300ms (rule: batch-window-p95). Incident created: INC-2026-1187.

maria:@sara can you ssh to gpu-12-03 and grab `dmesg | tail -n 50` and `rdma_diag -v`?

sara:paste below, quick scan: 
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:82:00.0: Uncommon NOP completion err, QP 0x1a3
[ 12345.679012] mlx5_core: qpn 4195 went to error state
```
and rdma_diag shows increasing retries on path 2.

ben:hmm. we've seen similar when MTU mismatch sneaks in via a host-level patch on a small subset of servers. check `ip link` MTU on both ends.

liz:also check `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` — if PMTU is oscillating and there's fragmentation it can blow up batch tail latency.

sara:mtu on gpu-12-03: 9000, gpu-12-07: 1500. whoops.

kyle:that explains it. jumbo on one side, default on the other -> fragment/drops, RDMA QP errors, and retries. any recent config pushes to rack-12?

maria:yes, we rolled a kernel/network driver patch to a subset of racks last night (rollout job: net-rollback-2026-03-19). looks like rack-12 picked it up early.

ben:we need a fast mitigation: either align MTU to 1500 across pair, or isolate the rack to stop cross-rack traffic using that path. can we BGP/ECMP drain the rack?

kyle:proposing temporary CNI policy to prefer spine-path that avoids rack-12 for pod-to-pod intra-node flows. That takes ~5-7min to propagate.

liz:+1 but quick fix: run `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500` on offending nodes to restore connectivity. I'll prepare a playbook.

sara:going to run the MTU change on gpu-12-03, gpu-12-04, gpu-12-05 one at a time and watch p95. doing gpu-12-03 now.

(2m later)

sara:gpu-12-03 mtu -> 1500 applied, restarting mlx driver not necessary. p95 dropped to 60ms within a minute. :thumbsup:

ben:good. please roll the rest of rack-12 nodes that still show 9000. also file a post-rollout check so we don't have config drift.

maria:agreed. i'm also going to add a preflight MTU detector to the rollout pipeline and block updates that change MTU without explicit approval.

kyle:for the incident, recommended follow-ups: (1) revert or pin the kernel patch for the rest of racks, (2) audit MTU drift over last 7 days, (3) add alert for mismatched MTU between RDMA peers.

liz:I've created a runbook snippet for next time and a short play to standardize MTU to 9000 cluster-wide if customer workload needs it, otherwise 1500. Will link runbook to INC-2026-1187.

infra-bot:INC-2026-1187 updated — status: mitigated (MTU aligned), actions: postmortem pending.

sara:closing notes: root cause was config drift from a partial kernel/driver rollout that reset some hosts to default MTU. symptomatic chain: MTU mismatch -> RDMA QP errors -> packet retransmits -> p95 spike during high-concurrency batch windows.

ben:great triage and quick mitigation. we'll schedule a blameless postmortem with the rollout owner. :calendar:

maria:adding action items to the rollout ticket now. thanks all.

kyle:lean follow-up: add an e2e synthetic that runs a small RDMA latency probe on canaries during network-rollouts.

sara:agree. thanks team, closing thread.
